description: Solo conceptual design team developing the MALS (Multi-pass Advanced Laser-dielectric System) deep-space observatory architecture for high-resolution deep-space and Planet X observation.
summary: The MALS (Multi-pass Advanced Laser-dielectric System) Observatory is a conceptual deep-space telescope architecture designed for Sun-Earth L2 orbit. To overcome vibration limits and launch size constraints, MALS introduces a deployable 21-meter conical optical tube (collapsing to 7.5 meters for launch) suspended coaxially via a 360-degree non-contact magnetic levitation (Maglev) system. Utilizing continuous rugate dielectric mirrors for multi-pass optical zoom, dual-AI autonomous governance, synthetic diamond thermal cooling, and a 5D quartz glass time capsule, MALS offers a resilient, nuclear-powered blueprint for next-generation deep-space observation and faint deep-space object detection such as Planet X.
